scope: Named foreign shareholders (≥1%) of five NIFTY 50 / large-cap constituents assigned as batch 1 — Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, Apollo Hospitals Enterprise, Asian Paints and Axis Bank — from primary SEBI Reg. 31(1)(b)/(c) shareholding-pattern filings opened directly on each company's own investor-relations site, plus LIC of India as the domestic control and the mandatory BlackRock/Vanguard/NBIM/GIC/Capital Group/Fidelity/KIA/ADIA comparison set tested against every company. Three of five companies (Adani Enterprises, Adani Ports, Axis Bank) rest on primary filings read table-by-table, including Table II promoter/promoter-group foreign entities and the Significant Beneficial Owner table. Two (Apollo Hospitals, Asian Paints) rest on screener.in aggregate data only, at tier reported: apollohospitals.com returned HTTP 403 on every route tried (the shareholding-pattern IR page and six guessed direct PDF URLs, with and without a browser user-agent), and asianpaints.com's shareholding-pattern page is a client-side JavaScript year-selector with no server-rendered PDF links reachable within budget. Two holders found in this batch sit outside SPEC's mandatory comparison set but are recorded per the domain instruction to name every foreign holder ≥1%: GQG Partners (already known from the base holders.json file, here concentrated in two Adani group companies specifically) and Dodge and Cox International Stock Fund (new, in Axis Bank). A promoter-group cluster of nine Mauritius/Cyprus/DMCC-registered 'Trade and Investment' shell vehicles recurs across Adani Enterprises' and Adani Ports' own Table II filings, categorized by the companies themselves as 'Promoter and Promoter Group (Foreign)' — distinct from the public Foreign Portfolio Investor lines, and recorded as such. A separate Abu Dhabi entity, International Holding Company PJSC (IHC, ADX-listed conglomerate), holds a public (non-promoter) 'Foreign Companies'-category stake in Adani Enterprises via a named subsidiary — recorded and explicitly distinguished from the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA, the emirate's sovereign wealth fund and a SPEC comparison-set member) per the institutions-not-bloodlines rule, since both are Abu Dhabi state-linked but are legally and institutionally separate actors. LIC of India is Axis Bank's sole promoter (not merely a public-shareholder domestic control) — a materially different relationship from LIC's public/DII holdings in the other companies checked, and flagged as such.
